identity.title: Stylus: Automatic Adapter Selection for Diffusion Models

problem.claim: Match image prompts to relevant adapters and compose them for high-quality generation.

gap.claim: The adapter ecosystem exceeds 100K items, most highly customized and insufficiently described, complicating selection.

contributions.claim: Stylus automatically selects and composes task-specific adapters from prompt keywords.
A three-stage pipeline improves adapter descriptions and embeddings, retrieves candidates, then assembles adapters by checking prompt fit.
StylusDocs is a curated dataset of 75K adapters with pre-computed embeddings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce an efficient, prompt-keyword-based system for automatic adapter selection and composition.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report greater CLIP/FID Pareto efficiency than the base model on popular Stable Diffusion checkpoints.
The authors report that Stylus was preferred twice as often as the base model, using humans and multimodal models as evaluators.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fine-tuned adapters offer lower-cost customization, and their open-source ecosystem has grown beyond 100K items with often inadequate descriptions.
The paper frames prompt-to-adapter matching and adapter composition as the route to higher-quality image generation.
Stylus selects and composes task-specific adapters through description and embedding improvement, retrieval, and prompt-fit-based assembly.
StylusDocs supports evaluation, where Stylus reportedly improves CLIP/FID Pareto efficiency and user/model preference over the base model.

source_observation.claim: The paper aligns its system stages with the data problem: inadequate adapter descriptions motivate improved descriptions and embeddings before retrieval and composition.

lessons.interpretation: A pipeline can make a selection claim more intelligible when each stage addresses a concrete bottleneck named in the problem framing.
lessons.application: When presenting a retrieval or selection system, map each processing stage explicitly to a stated source-data limitation, then evaluate the end-to-end outcome.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the abstract does not identify stage-specific bottlenecks or when the pipeline is not the main contribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact CLIP/FID values, preference protocol, baselines beyond the base model, or statistical uncertainty.
It does not detail how adapter descriptions, embeddings, prompt fit, or composition are implemented, nor the coverage of the Stable Diffusion checkpoints.
